svg.text: Day 7–9 runtime hardening
Normal population setup, role safety, real network topology, and packaged-process validation
Before review findings
Fixed runtime path
Population setup depended on a weak fixture path
A runtime volume could start at an unusable location and lack nav anchoring.
Ground/world-static overlap could reject every civilian spawn.
Civilian identity and config failures could be permissive
The base character supplied a combat identity even when a role should own it.
Malformed optional fields and class choices were not fully fail-closed.
Network/package checks could pass without proving topology
Day 7 wrappers did not assert the real role grant path.
Packaged mode could fall back to editor assumptions; launcher children could linger.
FireBolt client overlap could be treated as impact
The projectile needed an explicit source-avatar self-overlap guard.
The structural regression had to remain part of the final gate.
Nav-safe civilian population
Runtime fixture anchors to navigation, projects candidates, and checks pawn occupancy only.
Normal StartupMap flow registers the volume and finalizes canonical civilian members.
Role-owned, fail-closed identity and schema
Civilian defaults no longer grant a combat identity; role validation is exact and non-hostile.
Typed optional fields, ranges, classes, levels, and slot overrides are validated.
Authoritative topology and packaged proof
Listen/Dedicated runners exercise real clients, role grants, replication, late join, and respawn.
Packaged runner starts staged client/server launchers and tears down their full process trees.
FireBolt self-impact remains blocked
Source avatar, owner, and instigator overlaps are rejected before impact handling.
World collision behavior stays explicit and the graph contract passes.
Validation gate
25/25 native
Listen + Dedicated
Packaged PASS
3 UE builds
Static checks
FireBolt PASS
Evidence: AuraEditor, Aura, AuraServer Development builds; Day 7/8/9 network smokes; staged Windows client/server topology.
